To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed electrochemical enzyme-linked lectin-sorbent assays (ELLAs) using nanoporous gold as the solid support for the immobilization of glycoproteins and as an electrode to electrochemically determine the enzymatically generated p-aminophenoI product.
we have developed electrochemical assays for glycoprotein binding to lectin-enzyme conjugates using nanoporous gold.

we have developed a novel electrochemical enzyme-linked lectin-sorbent assay that uses nanoporous gold as an electrode for electrochemical determination of alkaline phosphatases substrate, p-aminophenylophosphate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of nanoporous materials for the development of novel electrochemical assays for proteins.
the development of electrochemical biosensors for the determination of glycoproteins and lectins.
the use of NPG as an electrode for square-wave voltammetric determination of p-AP, and the use of NGP as an electrode and a solid support for covalent immobilization of protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the electrochemical detection of enzymatically generated p-AP is an effective and convenient method to monitor the binding of lectins to glycoproteens and to determine the binding affinities of glycoproteins.
the use of nanoporous gold in combination with electrochemical detection is an effective approach to the development of electrochemical enzyme-linked lectin assays for the analysis of glycoproteins.
the ELLA developed here using NPG as a solid support, and as a working electrode, is a viable alternative to the ELISA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the feasibility of using NPG as a solid support to develop ELLA for the detection of glycoproteins.
we have demonstrated that nanoporous gold can be used for the immobilization of glycoproteins and lectins and as an electrode to electrochemically measure the product of an enzyme-substrate reaction.
we have developed electrochemical enzyme-linked lectin-sorbent assays for the detection of glycoproteins using a nanoporous gold electrode as the solid phase for protein immobilization.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a nanoporous gold electrode as an electrochemical transducer for enzyme-linked lectin assays provides a simple, inexpensive, and highly sensitive method to detect the presence and concentration of specific glycoproteins.
NPG is a promising solid support for the development of electrochemical assays for glycoprotein binding.
nanoporous gold is a promising material for the development of electrochemical enzyme-linked assays for glycoprotein detection.
